newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's S.Africa envoy sets to return on Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's S.Africa envoy sets to return on Sunday.

text.p: Taiwan formally recalled its ambassador to South Africa on Saturday in protest over Pretoria's recent decision to switch ties from Taipei to Beijing, the Foreign Ministry said.
Taiwan's Ambassador Loh I-cheng was expected to leave South Africa on Sunday and arrive in Taipei the next day, the state-funded Central News Agency said.

Foreign Minister John Chang, who made a recent trip to try to rescue ties with South Africa, announced last week that his nation would recall its ambassador to South Africa and immediately suspend all aid projects and treaties.
Chang has also assailed Pretoria for betraying its democratic ideals and bowing to pressure to switch recognition to China's "autocratic government".
South African President Nelson Mandela announced on November 27 that Pretoria, the biggest of Taiwan's 30 diplomatic allies, would switch ties to Beijing by the end of 1997.
Beijing's communist leaders have considered Taiwan a rebel province ever since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949 when the defeated Nationalists took refuge on the island.
Taipei, which has been trying to raise its international profile, sees Beijing's move to lure Pretoria as a further bid to isolate the island politically.
Taiwan's 30 allies are mostly underdeveloped states in the Pacific, Africa and central America that rely on it for aid.
